historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2022 79,990 -> FY2025 94,193; the only series not broken by the Aug-2023 Kenvue split-off or by talc reserve swings)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 5.2% vs revenue 5y 2.7% vs EPS 5y 14.8% -- all diverge >30%, none is a clean growth signal: the 5y revenue CAGR straddles the removal of ~15bn of Consumer Health revenue (Kenvue), FY2025 EPS of 11.13 carries a ~7bn pre-tax talc reserve reversal (FY2023's 13.88 carries the Kenvue gain), and equity was reduced by the Kenvue exchange offer. Ex-Kenvue continuing revenue compounded ~6.5%/yr FY2020-FY2025 (68.6bn -> 94.2bn).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC: FY2020 19,184; FY2022 16,047; FY2025 18,298). Owner and reported CAGRs are within 0.4pp because SBC is stable at ~1.3-1.5% of revenue; SBC is not outrunning cash flow. The 5-year FCF CAGR is negative because FY2020 still contained Consumer Health cash flow and FY2025 carried the largest transition-tax instalment.

scenario_narratives.base: JNJ delivers the low end of its 5-7% 2025-2030 operational growth ambition: FY2026 ~+7% (Caplyta annualising, FX, MedTech 5%+) then 5-5.5% as Stelara's ~7bn of lost sales is fully lapped by 2027 and Tremfya, Darzalex Faspro, Rybrevant-Lazcluze, Carvykti, Erleada and Spravato carry Innovative Medicine; growth decelerates from 2029 through the Darzalex IV, Imbruvica and Invega windows toward 2.5%. Cash EBITDA margin (after ~3bn/yr of litigation, restructuring and other cash costs outside adjusted earnings) improves 1pp to 34% as MedTech margins recover; cash tax normalises to 19.5% after the transition-tax roll-off. Talc is charged as a permanent cash drag rather than resolved. Terminal 18x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Pipeline and MedTech both deliver: growth stays at 6-7.5% through 2029, cash EBITDA reaches 36% by 2031, talc settles globally within the embedded drag, drug-pricing policy stays contained, terminal 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth stalls to ~1-2% from 2027 on MFN/negotiated pricing, tariffs and the Darzalex/Invega/Xarelto cliffs; talc keeps running through the courts and litigation cash rises; cash tax 21%; cash EBITDA 31%; terminal 15x. The business survives comfortably (bear-case FCF still ~20bn+), so this is a valuation bear, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: JNJ is valued as a mature, diversified cash compounder on strictly owner-FCF terms: SBC expensed, share count flat, litigation charged through the margin every year rather than adjusted away, cash tax normalised after the TCJA transition tax, and terminal value capped at 15-20x FCF so that the perpetuity does the work only the market has historically paid for. The house basis makes no allowance for multiple expansion beyond JNJ's own 15-20x EV/FCF history. At a 7% WACC the company is worth roughly what it earns discounted -- the question the required-return table answers is what return the current price, at ~30x owner FCF, actually offers.
key_risks_to_valuation: Talc litigation: ~60k ovarian/mesothelioma claims in the tort system after the third bankruptcy attempt (Red River) was rejected in March 2025; the model embeds ~3bn/yr of litigation and other cash drag indefinitely rather than a lump-sum reserve -- a global settlement materially above that, or a run of large verdicts, is downside not captured.

US drug pricing: Medicare negotiated prices for Xarelto and Stelara from 2026 and Imbruvica from 2027; most-favoured-nation pricing and Part D redesign; Darzalex and Tremfya are candidates for later negotiation rounds.
Patent cliffs inside the horizon: Stelara (in progress), Invega Sustenna and Xarelto (2026-27), Darzalex IV (~2029; Faspro conversion mitigates), Imbruvica, Erleada (early 2030s).
Pipeline execution: icotrokinra, TAR-200, nipocalimab, Rybrevant-Lazcluze uptake and Carvykti manufacturing scale-up underpin the 5-7% ambition; the bull case needs most of them.
Terminal-value dependence: the cap binds in all three cases, so the valuation is sensitive to the 15-20x exit assumption; PV of terminal is ~60% of enterprise value.
Balance-sheet vintage: net debt is the 2026-06-28 figure; JNJ is running 11-17bn of commercial paper after Intra-Cellular and Halda, so gross debt moves several billion a quarter.
Pharmaceutical tariffs and Pillar 2 minimum tax on the cash tax path; the base assumes ~19.5%, the bear 21%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 179.80-281.07
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000200406): 10-K FY2025 (period ended 2025-12-28) and 10-Q Q2 FY2026 (period ended 2026-06-28) for revenue, cash flow, D&A, SBC, buybacks, cash taxes, interest income/expense, debt and diluted shares; JNJ_Metrics.csv (research/JNJ/Reports) for the FY2007-Q2 2026 history.
data_sources.qualitative: JNJ_Analysis.json was not yet written when this valuation was built; scenario axes are drawn from the FY2025 10-K and Q2 FY2026 10-Q disclosures and the public record (talc/Red River, Stelara biosimilars, Kenvue separation, Abiomed/Shockwave/Intra-Cellular/Halda acquisitions, Medicare negotiation list).

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average DILUTED shares for the quarter ended 2026-06-28 (10-Q Q2 FY2026, us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding 2,440.1m; basic 2,407.4m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. Buybacks (FY2025 5,953m; H1-2026 4,249m) fund the flat count, so this is a paid-for convention, not a modelling assumption.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q2 FY2026 balance sheet (2026-06-28): long-term debt 37,344 + loans and notes payable (incl. commercial paper and current LTD) 11,692 = 49,036 gross; cash and equivalents 20,422 + marketable securities 336 = 20,758. NOTE: JNJ_Metrics.csv TotalDebt is inconsistent across periods -- FY rows double-count the current portion (FY2025 49,938 = LongTermDebt 41,438 + DebtCurrent 8,500; true 47,933) and quarterly rows carry LongTermDebtNoncurrent only (Q2 2026 37,344 omits 11,692 of short-term borrowings). The figures here are read directly from the SEC XBRL companyfacts tags.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was 1,056m but JNJ is a NET DEBTOR (net debt 28.3bn), so the cash-pile double-count the deduction guards against does not arise; reported FCF is roughly interest-neutral (interest income 1,056m vs interest expense 971m in FY2025) and is treated as the unlevered base. Not deducted.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 share-based compensation expense 1,400m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp; cash-flow add-back tag us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 1,354m). JNJ publishes no combined equity-award figure and no tax-withholding-on-net-settlement line is tagged; the P&L expense (the larger of the two) is used.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 payments for repurchase of common stock 5,953m; H1 FY2026 4,249m (Q1 4,028m). Dividends ~12.6bn/yr on top. Financing-activity cash, not an authorisation.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10y UST ~4.1-4.2%, ERP 5%, JNJ beta ~0.55 -> cost of equity ~6.9%; AAA/AA-rated debt at ~4.6% pre-tax, ~7% of capital -> WACC ~6.7%, rounded up to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; scenario risk is charged through the probability weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial (<0.5% of revenue); lease cost left inside EBITDA, lease liabilities excluded from net debt (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.litigation_treatment: Talc (ovarian/mesothelioma, ~60k+ claims after the Red River bankruptcy plan was rejected in March 2025, which triggered a ~7bn reserve reversal in Q1 FY2025), opioid and other litigation cash is charged through the EBITDA margin: the FY2025 underlying pre-SBC EBITDA margin was ~36.5% of revenue (GAAP pretax ex-reversal 25.6bn + D&A 7.5bn + SBC 1.4bn), and the base path starts at 33.0%, i.e. a ~3.3bn/yr haircut for litigation settlements, restructuring and other cash costs that sit outside adjusted earnings. Consistent with the persistent 4-5bn/yr gap between adjusted-NI + D&A - capex and reported FCF in FY2024-25. The accrued litigation reserve is therefore NOT deducted in the equity bridge (that would charge it twice).
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes 6,539m included the final (25%) instalment of the TCJA transition tax (~2.7bn; FY2024's 6,714m carried the 20% instalment). Underlying cash rate ~17% of EBIT. OBBBA restored immediate US R&D expensing from 2025 (lowers 2026-27 cash tax); Pillar 2 and the loss of the transition-tax-free base push the rate toward 19.5% by year 5. Book amortisation of acquired intangibles (~4.6bn/yr, mostly from stock deals without a tax step-up) is largely non-deductible, so the engine's D&A tax shield is overstated; the cash tax path is set ~1pp above JNJ's adjusted effective rate to compensate.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: US operating company, pharma/medtech). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY entry. Analysis JSON not yet available at build time; narrative drawn from the 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026 disclosures and the public record. Post-Kenvue (2023) pure-play Innovative Medicine (~64% of sales) + MedTech (~36%). Revenue base FY2025 94,193m; H1 FY2026 revenue 49,372m, +8.2% y/y (Q2 +6.6%) with an FX tailwind and Intra-Cellular (Caplyta, closed April 2025) annualising, against Stelara biosimilar erosion (Stelara ~10.4bn FY2024 -> ~6.5bn FY2025 -> ~3.5-4bn FY2026). Owner FCF FY2025 = 19,698 - 1,400 = 18,298m (19.4% of revenue). Year-1 owner FCF from the component build is ~22.6bn (22.4%); the step-up from FY2025 is the ~2.7bn transition-tax roll-off plus ~7% revenue growth, and it is below the ~24-25bn a reported-FCF bridge from guided adjusted EPS would give. Price is the 2026-09-28 regular close, not an after-hours print. Historical CAGRs on the reported basis are polluted by the Kenvue separation (FY2023 revenue/equity break) and by talc reserve swings in FY2023/FY2025 net income; the 3-year revenue CAGR (5.6%, all post-Kenvue-like continuing mix) is the cleanest anchor.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance, then growth stalls: most-favoured-nation pricing and expanded Medicare negotiation bite from 2027 (Xarelto, Stelara, Imbruvica already listed; Darzalex, Tremfya, Erleada in the next rounds), pharma tariffs and Pillar 2 lift the cash tax rate to 21%, Invega Sustenna and Xarelto go generic with Stelara, Darzalex IV LOE arrives in 2029 with Faspro conversion incomplete, and one of icotrokinra / nipocalimab / TAR-200 disappoints. Talc does not settle: individual trials continue with periodic nine-figure verdicts and defence costs run above the ~3bn/yr embedded, compressing the cash EBITDA margin to 31%. MedTech stays a 3-4% grower in a price-pressured hospital market. Terminal at 15x, the bottom of the historical range.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.0% on H1 +8.2% (FX tailwind fading, Stelara still eroding in H2; management's July guidance implied ~100.5-101bn reported). FY2027-28 5-5.5%: Stelara washed out, Tremfya/Darzalex Faspro/Rybrevant-Lazcluze/Carvykti/Caplyta/Spravato and MedTech (Shockwave, Abiomed, Ottava launch) carry growth; Invega Sustenna and Xarelto (Medicare negotiated price from 2026) erode. FY2029+ decelerates through the Darzalex IV/Imbruvica/Erleada patent window toward 2.5% terminal. Sits at the bottom of JNJ's stated 5-7% 2025-2030 ambition.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC, post-litigation-cash EBITDA margin 33.0% -> 34.0% by year 3 and held: Stelara (very high margin) loss is offset by MedTech margin recovery and Innovative Medicine mix; the ~3pp haircut versus the FY2025 underlying 36.5% is the recurring litigation/restructuring/other cash drag (see inputs.litigation_treatment).
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 8.0% of revenue in FY2025 (7,503m, of which 4,600m acquired-intangible amortisation) glides to 6.5% as Actelion/Abiomed/Shockwave/Intra-Cellular amortisation runs off; capex 5.2% (FY2025 5.1%; JNJ's 55bn 4-year US manufacturing pledge) eases to 4.5%. Terminal D&A > capex by 2pp reflects non-cash intangible amortisation, not under-investment; the tax path compensates for the largely non-deductible portion.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + inventory (~28bn) exceed payables (~10bn); growth consumes ~8% of the revenue increase.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 7.0%/2.5% implies 22.8x year-10 FCF; capped at 18x, the middle of JNJ's 15-20x historical EV/FCF range. The cap binds in the base case.

bull.narrative: Top of the 5-7% ambition and beyond it into the 2030s: Tremfya reaches 10bn+ in IBD, icotrokinra (oral IL-23) and TAR-200/nipocalimab launch on time, Rybrevant-Lazcluze becomes standard of care in EGFR lung, Carvykti moves to earlier lines, Caplyta wins the adjunctive MDD label; MedTech accelerates to 6-7% with Ottava and cardiovascular (Shockwave, Impella) mix, lifting group EBITDA to 36%. Talc resolves through a global settlement inside the modelled ~3bn/yr cash drag, and US drug-pricing policy (MFN, Part D redesign) stays at the margin. Terminal at 20x, the top of JNJ's historical range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because two independent, policy-driven tails sit outside management's control -- US drug-pricing policy (MFN, Medicare negotiation reaching JNJ's largest brands by 2028) and unresolved talc litigation with ~60k claims now proceeding case-by-case after the Red River plan was rejected -- and the Darzalex patent window opens inside the horizon. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three things to go right at once: the 2025-27 launch cohort (icotrokinra, TAR-200, nipocalimab, Rybrevant), MedTech re-acceleration on Ottava/cardiovascular, and a benign pricing environment. Base at 50%: JNJ's diversification, AAA balance sheet and 60+ year dividend record make the central path the most likely by a wide margin.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
